source.notes: Scanned school paper with no text layer (only the icseboard.org watermark); OCR corrected against the page images. No year is printed on the paper; examYear 2025 is taken from the file name (...-070325-2025) and the icseboard.org folder. Printed header: GRADE- VI, HISTORY, ASSESSMENT-II, M.M-80, TIME 2 HOUR. The paper covers History and Civics (Part II Section A is Civics) and has no Geography section. Where only a group total is printed it is divided evenly among the items (marksSource SECTION_INSTRUCTIONS). Q5 and Q10 are 'any 5' of 6 items and Q11 is 'any 1' of 2, so the listed marks (87) exceed 80. Handwritten strike-throughs (Q1 option 10a, Q6.3) and a tick mark near Q11 are ignored; the printed text is kept. The paper's own spellings (e.g. 'Muncipal', 'Majanapadas', 'Diference') are kept.

questions.text:
Read the passage given below and answer the question that follow?
About 200 years ago some janapadas became more important than others and were known as Mahajanapadas. Most Mahajanpadas had a capital city many of these were fortified. This means that huge walls of wood, brick and stone were built around them.
1.What was the capital of Magadh?
a)Ramgraha b)Rajgriha c)Rameswara d)Ratnapur
2.Why were the Mahajanpadas fortified?
a)To protect the Kingdom from enemy b) To protect the Kingdom from natural calamities c) To protect the Kingdom from wild animals d) To protect the Kingdom from snakes
3)Taxes were now being imposed on people by the rulers for
a) maintaining a large army b)paying the officers assisting the king c)fortification of the kingdom d) all of these
4) Most powerful territories in the 6th century were referred to as ____
extractionIssues: Passage-based question kept together (stem + four parts) under the printed (4)
OCR text corrected against the page image
